aliases: Whipple 10 m imaging atmospheric Cherenkov telescope

facility_roles.quote: The Whipple 10 m gamma-ray telescope was located at the Fred Lawrence Whipple Observatory in Southern Arizona in the United States.

intervals.label: construction
intervals.note: The timeline dates the installation of the telescope at Mt. Hopkins to 1966-68; the Whipple page dates operation from 1968.
intervals.quote: 1966-68 Fazio and Weekes: Installation of SAO's Whipple 10m telescope at Mt. Hopkins; first purpose-built large reflector for TeV Gamma-ray Astronomy

intervals.label: operation
intervals.note: Operating span of the telescope. The gamma-ray programme was closed down in 1976-82 (separate interval); the first TeV source (the Crab Nebula) was detected in 1989 with the imaging camera installed in 1984.
intervals.quote: this telescope was in operation from 1968 until its decommissioning in 2013

intervals.label: gamma-ray programme closed down
intervals.note: The timeline says the Whipple/SAO gamma-ray programme closed down 1976-82 and that TeV gamma-ray astronomy then entered the "Dark Ages"; the gamma-ray programme was constituted again as the Whipple Collaboration in 1982.

intervals.label: telescope decommissioned
intervals.quote: this telescope was in operation from 1968 until its decommissioning in 2013

quantity.quote: The Davies-Cotton reflector held 248 hexagonal mirrors and provided a total reflecting area of 75 m^2.

key_specs.label: Lower end of operating energy range

quantity.quote: The telescope operated between 300 GeV and 10 TeV.

name: Whipple 10 m Gamma-Ray Telescope
notes: Successor: the Whipple page calls the 10 m telescope the predecessor of VERITAS. The matching lineage row (predecessor, on experiment:veritas) belongs to the VERITAS record and is left to the integrator.
The first extragalactic TeV source (Markarian 421, 1992) and the first TeV source (Crab, 1989) are recorded as results.
Facility record note: the host facility's own intervals start in 2003 (VERITAS); the 10 m telescope predates them (validator warning A12 is expected).
No INSPIRE experiment id is recorded: INSPIRE was not contacted by this stream.

physics_goals.quote: The primary emphasis of the collaboration's research effort was the search for and study of gamma ray sources in the energy range of 100 GeV - 10 TeV.
physics_goals.value: Search for and study gamma-ray sources in the energy range of 100 GeV to 10 TeV.

summary.plain: The 10 metre mirror on Mount Hopkins, Arizona, that in 1989 detected the first source of TeV gamma rays, the Crab Nebula, and founded imaging Cherenkov astronomy. It ran from 1968 until 2013 and led to VERITAS.
summary.technical: Whipple 10 m Davies-Cotton imaging atmospheric Cherenkov telescope at the Fred Lawrence Whipple Observatory (75 m2 reflector of 248 mirrors, camera up to 379 PMTs, 300 GeV-10 TeV). First TeV source (Crab, 1989) and first extragalactic TeV source (Mrk 421, 1992). Operated 1968-2013; predecessor of VERITAS.

unique_capabilities.quote: The Whipple collaboration pioneered the Imaging Atmospheric Cherenkov Technique (IACT) for the detection of Very High Energy (VHE) gamma rays.
unique_capabilities.value: Pioneered the imaging atmospheric Cherenkov technique for detecting very high energy gamma rays; detected the first TeV gamma-ray source, the Crab Nebula, in 1989.
